facts: The Taj Mahal is a mausoleum built in memory of Mumtaz Mahal.
Shah Jahan commissioned the Taj Mahal beside the Yamuna River.
The Taj Mahal's main tomb stands at one end of its garden rather than in the centre.
The Taj Mahal's decorative flowers include coloured stones inlaid into white marble.
The Taj Mahal's central burial chamber has an octagonal plan.
A carved marble lattice surrounds the Taj Mahal's two ceremonial tomb markers.
Craftspeople from Central Asia and Iran helped build the Taj Mahal.
The Taj Mahal complex includes a mosque and a matching guest house.
The Taj Mahal's surrounding buildings were completed after the main mausoleum.
Arabic inscriptions on the Taj Mahal helped historians establish its construction chronology.
Petra was a caravan crossroads linking Arabian incense, Chinese silk and Indian spices.
Petra's Nabataean builders carved some buildings into rock and constructed others separately.
Petra's water-storage network made a substantial city possible in an arid landscape.
The winding passage called the Siq forms Petra's famous eastern entrance.
Petra's architecture combines local Nabataean traditions with Greek-inspired designs.
Petra's ruins include churches from the Byzantine period.
Petra's builders used dams to divert water as well as cisterns to store it.
Many of Petra's spectacular carved façades belong to tombs.
Petra's Urn Tomb was later converted into a church.
Archaeological remains around Petra include prehistoric settlements and ancient copper mining.
China's Great Wall is a collection of fortifications built across many centuries.
The Great Wall includes horse tracks, shelters and fortresses as well as walls.
Some ancient Great Wall sections were made of compacted earth.
The Great Wall's familiar masonry sections include major work from the Ming dynasty.
The Great Wall's defensive system included beacon towers for signalling.
Successive Chinese empires worked on the Great Wall from antiquity into the seventeenth century.
The full Great Wall network extends for more than 20,000 kilometres.
Mountain passes were important fortified points in the Great Wall system.
The Great Wall's construction and human cost became themes in Chinese poetry.
The Great Wall's western fortifications reach the Gansu region, far from Beijing.
Angkor is an extensive former urban landscape, not just the temple Angkor Wat.
Angkor's builders engineered large reservoirs and canals.
People still live and farm within the Angkor archaeological park.
Angkor served as the centre of the Khmer kingdom for centuries.
The Angkor archaeological area covers roughly 400 square kilometres.
Angkor contains temples built across several centuries, rather than in a single construction campaign.
The Bayon and Ta Prohm are part of the wider Angkor complex.
Angkor's great reservoirs are known as barays.
Khmer architecture developed Indian influences into a distinctive regional style.
Rice cultivation remains part of life in Angkor's villages.
Taos Pueblo's earthen buildings rise as high as five storeys.
Taos Pueblo is a living community, not an abandoned archaeological site.
Taos Pueblo's multi-storey homes are built from adobe.
Taos Pueblo's buildings form stepped terraces, with upper floors set back.
A stream fed by sacred Blue Lake passes through Taos Pueblo.
Taos Pueblo includes underground ceremonial chambers called kivas.
Taos Pueblo has been continuously inhabited for centuries.
The Taos Pueblo site includes a traditional foot-racing track.
Taos Pueblo preserves both the ruins of an early church and a later church.
Traditional building methods help Taos Pueblo retain its distinctive earthen architecture.
Ellora's rock-cut monuments include Buddhist, Hindu and Jain sanctuaries together.
Ellora's Kailasa temple was carved from rock rather than assembled from separate stone blocks.
Ellora includes a three-storey Buddhist monastery carved into the hillside.
One Ellora sculpture depicts Ravana trying to lift Mount Kailasa.
Ellora's rock-cut temples still preserve traces of painted decoration.
The famous Ellora ensemble contains 34 numbered caves.
Ellora's Buddhist, Hindu and Jain caves were created in successive, partly overlapping phases.
Ellora's Cave 10 is nicknamed the Carpenter's Cave.
Ellora's Jain caves include exceptionally delicate carved figures.
The Kailasa temple translates the appearance of constructed architecture into a single rock-cut monument.
Borobudur was built around a natural hill.
Borobudur's upper circular platforms contrast with its square lower terraces.
Seventy-two openwork stupas surround Borobudur's upper platforms.
Borobudur's smaller perforated stupas each shelter a Buddha figure.
Borobudur's rising levels symbolise stages in Buddhist cosmology.
Borobudur's carved reliefs cover thousands of square metres.
Borobudur, Mendut and Pawon temples lie along a shared axis.
Borobudur combines Buddhist ideas with an older tradition of sacred terraced mountains.
Borobudur was abandoned for centuries before major modern restoration.
A large central stupa crowns Borobudur's stepped structure.
The Acropolis was fortified long before the Parthenon was built.
An earlier Mycenaean ruler's residence stood on the Acropolis hill.
The Parthenon is only one of several temples on the Athenian Acropolis.
Athena was worshipped on the Acropolis as Athens' patron goddess.
The grand entrance to the Acropolis is called the Propylaia.
Pericles led the major fifth-century BCE building programme on the Acropolis.
The Acropolis monuments survived changing religious uses as well as wars and earthquakes.
The Athenian Acropolis is steep on nearly every side but has a relatively flat summit.
Acropolis architecture inspired neoclassical buildings far beyond Greece.
The Parthenon was built between 447 and 432 BCE.
